description: Outline application (Scale and Layout Only) for the demolition of garage to the rear of 147 Eastcote Lane and construction of a two storey building with accommodation in the roof space to provide five self contained flats. All matters reserved save for Scale and Layout
decision_conditions:
<p><span style="font-size:11.0pt;line-height:107%;
font-family:&quot;Aptos&quot;,sans-serif;mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-fareast-font-family:
Aptos;mso-fareast-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin;
mso-bidi-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi;
mso-ansi-language:EN-GB;mso-fareast-language:EN-US;mso-bidi-language:AR-SA">The
applicant has failed to provide a transport assessment including details of
existing car ownership levels or a parking survey to demonstrate the impact the
proposed development could have on on-street parking demand for a road that
already experiences high levels of parking stress due to the absence of a
controlled parking zone. In the absence of this information, the Local Planning
Authority cannot be satisfied that the proposal would not result in increased
pressure on the limited on-street parking available to the detriment of
existing residents and the safe and efficient operation of the surrounding
highway network. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies T4 and T6 of
the London Plan, Policy CS1 of the Core Strategy and Policy DM42 of the Harrow Development
Management Policies Local Plan (2013).</span></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style=""><span style="text-indent: -18pt;">The
proposal fails to demonstrate how it would achieve the statutory minimum 10%
Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG), as required by the Environment Act 2021. In the
absence of this information, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied
that the development would not result in a net loss of biodiversity or that it
would deliver the required net gain. The proposal is therefore contrary to the
National Planning Policy Framework (2024),&nbsp;Policy G6 of the London Plan
(2021), policy CS1E of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and&nbsp; policies DM20
and DM21 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).</span></p><p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-align:justify;text-indent:-18.0pt;
mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The proposal, by virtue of its excessive scale, height, width and siting within the plot, would give rise to development of excessive bulk and mass which would fail to respect the prevailing character and pattern of development of the surrounding area and would therefore be harmful to the character and visual amenity of the surrounding street scene and area,&nbsp; contrary to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D3.D(1), D3.D(7) and D3.D(11) of the London Plan (2021), policy DM1 of the Harrow Development Management Policies 2013, the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide 2010.</p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The proposal, by reason of its excessive bulk, scale, massing, siting and the potential for overlooking and perception of overlooking as a result of proposed balcony at roof level on the northern elevation, would have an have an unacceptable impact on the residential amenities of neighbouring occupiers in terms of loss of privacy, outlook, and overshadowing to amenity areas, and an overbearing impact on the amenity space of No. 147, to the detriment of the residential amenities of occupiers of the neighbouring properties at No.147 Eastcote Lane and No.149 Eastcote Lane, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D3.D(7) of The London Plan (2021),&nbsp; policy DM1 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013), the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide Supplementary Planning Document (2010).</p>
